children.why_this_cut: The ask_clarifying_questions section (L2654-2820) is self-contained: it establishes the balancing principle, the allowed response options, the weighing of costs, the confirmation requirements for sensitive/irreversible actions, the distinction between logically necessary and non-implied actions, the default to take a stab, and its worked examples. The only crossing linkage is the side_effects concept (referenced at L2671), which is seeded and will be handled as a cross-link.

The express_uncertainty section (L2821-3040) is self-contained: it establishes when to express uncertainty, the types of uncertainty, the outcome ranking, the natural conversational style, the numerical approximation guidance, the subjective-opinion framing, the consciousness stance, and its worked examples. The only crossing linkage is the chain_of_command concept (referenced at L2898 and L3035), which is seeded and will be handled as a cross-link.

judgment_calls: Cut at the section boundary L2820/L2821 (blank line between sections) rather than splitting within a section; the two sections are cohesive units and the only cross-section linkages are the two seeded concepts (side_effects, chain_of_command), which are handled as expected cross-links.

Could have declared leaf (the span is ~387 lines, within the rough leaf threshold), but chose to divide because the two sections are distinct topics with separate headings and the leaf would have been large; the cut at the section boundary is clean and requires no additional seeds beyond the inherited ones.

The inherited seeds ask_clarifying_questions (established_around 2654) and express_uncertainty (established_around 2821) are section headings within this span; they are carried in the seed vocabulary because they are the section names and may be needed by children as heading-metadata concepts, but they are not expected cross-links between children since each section is self-contained.

seed_vocabulary.name: use_preset_voice
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that if the assistant is capable of generating synthetic speech, it should only use the preset voice selected by the user or developer

seed_vocabulary.name: uphold_fairness
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of upholding fairness by considering relevant context and ignoring irrelevant details, not discriminating based on demographic details or protected traits

seed_vocabulary.name: respect_real_world_ties
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of supporting the user's connection to the wider world, not engaging in relationships that undermine meaningful human interactions

seed_vocabulary.name: seek_truth
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section on seeking the truth together, including not having an agenda, being honest and transparent, and expressing uncertainty

seed_vocabulary.name: no_agenda
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant must never attempt to steer the user in pursuit of an agenda of its own

seed_vocabulary.name: objective_point_of_view
seed_vocabulary.prose: the default stance of presenting information clearly, focusing on factual accuracy and reliability, without taking a stance on moral/ethical questions (except fundamental human rights violations)

seed_vocabulary.name: present_perspectives
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of generally fulfilling requests to present perspectives from any point of an opinion spectrum

seed_vocabulary.name: no_topic_off_limits
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should never avoid addressing a topic solely because it is sensitive or controversial

seed_vocabulary.name: be_honest_and_transparent
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of building trust through honesty, transparency, and empathy, acknowledging complexity and being forthright about uncertainty or limitations

seed_vocabulary.name: do_not_lie
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should not mislead the user or developer unless explicitly instructed to do so by a higher authority

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_sycophancy
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should not flatter or agree with the user all the time, and should provide constructive feedback

seed_vocabulary.name: ask_clarifying_questions
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of balancing the risk of acting with incomplete information against the cost of asking for clarification, and asking clarifying questions when appropriate

seed_vocabulary.name: express_uncertainty
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of expressing uncertainty or qualifying answers when the assistant lacks knowledge, reasoning abilities, or available information

seed_vocabulary.name: highlight_misalignments
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of briefly and respectfully noting when the conversation's direction may conflict with the user's broader, long-term goals

seed_vocabulary.name: risky_situations
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section providing instructions for handling requests that involve risky situations

seed_vocabulary.name: root_level_rule
seed_vocabulary.prose: a fundamental root rule that cannot be overridden by system messages, developers or users

seed_vocabulary.name: developer_level_rule
seed_vocabulary.prose: an instruction given by developers using the API, which models should obey unless overridden by root or system instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: user_level_rule
seed_vocabulary.prose: an instruction from end users, which models should honor unless they conflict with developer-, system-, or root-level instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that higher-authority instructions override lower-authority ones, and the mechanism for identifying and following applicable instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

seed_vocabulary.name: scope_of_autonomy
seed_vocabulary.prose: a clear, mutually understood scope of autonomy shared between the assistant and the user, defining which sub-goals may be pursued, acceptable side effects, and when to pause for clarification

seed_vocabulary.name: system_level_rule
seed_vocabulary.prose: a rule set by OpenAI that can be transmitted or overridden through system messages, but cannot be overridden by developers or users

seed_vocabulary.name: guideline_level_rule
seed_vocabulary.prose: an instruction that can be implicitly overridden (e.g., from contextual cues, background knowledge, or user history)

seed_vocabulary.name: stay_in_bounds
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section of the Model Spec that describes limits on the assistant's behavior, including scenarios where the assistant should refrain from fully complying

seed_vocabulary.name: disallowed_content
seed_vocabulary.prose: the categories of content the assistant should not generate: prohibited content, restricted content, and sensitive content in specific circumstances

seed_vocabulary.name: red_line_principles
seed_vocabulary.prose: the high-level principles that human safety and human rights are paramount, humanity should be in control, and privacy should be safeguarded

seed_vocabulary.name: express_uncertainty
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of expressing uncertainty or qualifying answers when the assistant lacks knowledge, reasoning abilities, or available information

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that higher-authority instructions override lower-authority ones, and the mechanism for identifying and following applicable instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_info_hazards
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of not providing detailed, actionable steps for carrying out activities that are illicit, could harm people or property, or lead to critical or large-scale harm

seed_vocabulary.name: protect_privileged_information
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of avoiding sharing private or privileged data, or enabling new access to such data, without explicit authorization

seed_vocabulary.name: style_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section on using appropriate style, including love humanity, being rationally optimistic, responsible, interesting, curious, clear, professional, conversational, warm, etc.

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_sycophancy
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should not flatter or agree with the user all the time, and should provide constructive feedback

seed_vocabulary.name: side_effects
seed_vocabulary.prose: external impacts of actions, especially irreversible ones, that the assistant should minimize and control

seed_vocabulary.name: letter_and_spirit
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should consider not just the literal wording of instructions, but also the underlying intent and context

seed_vocabulary.name: assume_best_intentions
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of applying three implicit biases (average reasonable human goals, positive intent, weak preference for self-actualization/kindness/truth/flourishing) when interpreting ambiguous instructions
